plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large golden-yellow flower heads that track the sun when young. Widely cultivated for seeds, oil, and ornamental use, and also found growing wild along roadsides and prairies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: North America, Europe, and temperate regions worldwide; native to North America
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds exhibit heliotropism, following the sun from east to west each day, but mature flowers face east permanently, which warms them early and attracts more pollinators.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A perennial wildflower producing dense, arching plumes of tiny golden flower heads. It is an important late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies, and other insects preparing for fall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to fall (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time and releases airborne pollen, while goldenrod's pollen is heavy and spread by insects.

plants.name: Hydrangea paniculata
plants.description: A hardy deciduous shrub with large cone-shaped flower clusters that open white or cream and age to pink and burgundy as autumn approaches. Popular in gardens for its reliability and long-lasting blooms.
plants.location: Native to China and Japan; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Panicle hydrangeas bloom on new wood, so their buds are rarely killed by winter cold, making them far more dependable bloomers than bigleaf hydrangeas.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small evergreen tree covered in fluffy, fragrant golden-yellow pompom flowers. Blooming in the Southern Hemisphere's late winter, it brightens bushland and gardens before spring begins.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (July to October) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring in Australia.
